title: Unlimited: No Player Limit
description:
Play [b]Slay the Spire 2[/b] multiplayer with up to 16 players.

The vanilla game caps lobbies at 4; this mod raises the cap to 16 and lets you configure it from the in-game settings menu.

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*]Set max players from 2 to 16 via the in-game Settings menu
[*]Changes save automatically
[*]Supports both Steam lobbies and direct IP (ENet) connections
[*]Scales enemy difficulty to match your player count
[*]Optional: override the player count used for difficulty scaling (1–16), independent of how many are actually connected — including an optional toggle to apply it in singleplayer as a challenge mode. In multiplayer the host's value applies to everyone.
[*]Lightweight: Harmony patches only — no game file modifications
[/list]

[b]All players in the lobby must have the mod installed.[/b]

[h2]Recommended Mods[/h2]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3747532120]Vanilla and Modded Saves Merger[/url] — unifies your save directory so modded and vanilla play share the same progression.

[h2]Configuration[/h2]
Open [b]Settings[/b] in-game and use the [b]Max Players[/b] slider (range: 2–16). Changes save automatically. The default is 8 players.

16 is a hard limit, not a slider preference: the mod widens the lobby packet's player-list header to a fixed width sized for 16 players so that every peer agrees on the wire format. Forcing a higher number through the config file is not supported and will break lobbies.

If you want to set the count without launching the game, edit [i]sts2unlimited.settings.json[/i] next to the mod's files (for example [i]{"MaxPlayers": 8}[/i]) and restart.
changeNote:
Fixes Difficulty Scaling not affecting enemy block on game v0.113.

Game build v0.113 moved the class that scales monster block for multiplayer, so the mod could no longer find it. Enemy HP still scaled, but block fell back to the vanilla player count: at Difficulty Scaling 9 with 2 players, 10 block came out as 20 instead of 99. Block now scales with your Difficulty Scaling value again.

The mod also now reports this kind of break clearly. If a game update moves something the difficulty patches depend on, the mod loads as DEGRADED and names the patch, instead of loading normally with a single warning in the log.

The release no longer ships sts2unlimited.maxplayers.txt. Settings live in sts2unlimited.settings.json, which the mod writes when you change a setting in-game; an existing maxplayers.txt is still read.

Everyone in the lobby should be on this version.
